threats.title: Phishing
threats.definition: A social engineering attack that tricks people into revealing sensitive information or installing malware by impersonating trusted entities.
threats.how: Attackers send fake emails, messages or create look-alike websites that ask for credentials, payment details or downloads.
prevention: Never enter passwords from email links
ifAffected: Change passwords immediately from a clean device
Contact your bank if financial data was shared

threats.title: Malware
threats.definition: Malicious software designed to damage, disrupt, or gain unauthorized access to systems.
threats.how: Often delivered via email attachments, malicious downloads, infected USB drives or compromised websites.
ifAffected: Restore from clean backup if necessary
Seek professional help for severe cases

threats.title: Ransomware
threats.definition: Malware that encrypts files and demands payment for the decryption key.
threats.how: Usually enters through phishing, remote desktop vulnerabilities or malicious downloads, then encrypts data.
ifAffected: Do not pay immediately — report and seek advice

threats.title: Social Engineering
threats.definition: Psychological manipulation of people into performing actions or divulging confidential information.
threats.how: Attackers exploit trust, fear, urgency or curiosity through phone, email, chat or in person.

threats.title: Identity Theft
threats.definition: Stealing personal information to impersonate someone for financial or other gain.
threats.how: Through data breaches, phishing, malware, physical document theft or social media oversharing.

threats.title: DDoS Attacks
threats.definition: Distributed Denial of Service — overwhelming a service with traffic so legitimate users cannot access it.
threats.how: Attackers use many compromised devices (botnet) to flood a target with requests.
signs: Website or service becomes very slow or unavailable
